requirement: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Outline inputs recorded from selected search snippets under {cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs` MUST count alongside mandatory inputs and additional reads. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap for `requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`. Each obligation maps to a test with assertions that enforce the expected outcome.

**Which files are parsed**
- `src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reports_all_files_and_parse_failures]` builds a project and asserts which files are scanned.
  - Skipped: root `vendor/`, root `book/` and `evidence/`, `.git/`, and `target/` at any depth.
  - Scanned: `src/vendor/own.rs`, `src/book/own.rs`, `src/evidence/check.rs` and `tests/broken.rs`.
  - It asserts that `tests/broken.rs` produces a "cannot parse Rust source" error, and that this is the only error. The uncovered items are reported separately as warnings.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[discovery_errors_fail_before_configuration_or_inference]` checks that a Rust parse failure is reported with its file location and fails the run.
- `tests/references.rs#fn[disallowed_paths_are_skipped_and_projects_outside_git_scan_every_file]` and `#fn[untracked_sources_are_not_validated_until_staged_and_status_lists_them]` cover the discovery set: Git-index and non-Git behaviour, and the root `vendor` exclusion.

**Which items can be covered**
- `fn[checks_trait_test_helper_and_nested_functions_separately]` covers trait methods, test helpers, nested functions, and `{test}` references to a requirement or named example.
- `fn[structs_enums_and_unions_need_references_attached_or_inside]` covers structs, enums and unions. It also covers a reference before a field, variant or attribute inside an item, and a nested struct in a function.

**Reference forms that cover an item**
- `fn[finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references]` and `fn[locates_functions_after_unicode_text]` check these cases:
  - attached and body comments, and inner and outer doc comments;
  - a trailing same-line comment;
  - a comment run across a blank line;
  - an unknown requirement name, which does not cover the item;
  - references inside string and raw-string literals, which do not count;
  - references on an enclosing module or impl block, which do not cover the items inside.
- `fn[an_example_counts_only_when_it_references_a_requirement]` and `fn[a_test_reference_to_an_example_counts_only_when_it_references_a_requirement]` check the named-example rule. An example with `{test}` to a requirement counts. An example with no requirement, one that only cites another example, or one that only cites a term does not. A reference to a term does not cover an item.
- `tests/references.rs#fn[fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated]` and `#fn[habeas_util_citations_cover_their_item_without_a_citation_review]` check `habeas:util`.
  - Inline and fenced `{cite}` forms cover the item.
  - `{impl}` and `{test}` of `habeas:util` do not cover it.
  - Unknown built-ins and a wrong role are rejected.
  - A fenced citation with no closing fence is reported.
- `fn[a_fixme_does_not_count_as_an_items_reference]` checks that a `{fixme}` does not cover an item.

**Coverage by evidence reads**
- `fn[a_read_covers_an_item_only_with_its_current_hash]` and `fn[a_containing_read_covers_nested_items_only_with_its_current_hash]` check the hash rule.
  - A current hash covers the item and, through a containing node, its nested items.
  - A stale hash, an unrelated item and a different file do not.
- Evidence records, citation reviews and site reviews all go through `EvidenceReads::load`, which loads every `.json` file under `evidence/`. `add_record` reads their `inputs`.
  - `tests/references.rs#fn[items_named_by_recent_evidence_have_recent_coverage_whatever_their_hash]` exercises all three kinds, including an impl block containing a method.
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[replacing_a_record_that_stops_reading_an_item_warns_until_it_is_covered]` exercises the end-to-end effect of an ordinary record.
- Search-snippet inputs are stored as ordinary `inputs` entries in the record. The `src/authoring/mod.rs` test `a_helper_used_only_through_a_search_snippet_invalidates_saved_evidence_when_weakened` shows the snippet input in `evidence["inputs"]`. That test is assessed under `requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs`. Counting those inputs needs no separate path in `EvidenceReads`.

**Errors versus warnings**
- `reports_all_files_and_parse_failures` asserts that uncovered functions are returned as warnings, not errors.
- `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form]` checks that status reports the warning count by default and lists the warnings only with `--coverage`.

**Possible tension, judged not a gap**
`items_named_by_recent_evidence_have_recent_coverage_whatever_their_hash` accepts a stale hash as "recent coverage". That is the `coverage.history` warning filter, which sits on top of the "covered" notion. The unit tests assert that coverage by an evidence read requires the current hash. The two assertions concern different layers, so I did not treat this as a wrong expected result.

**Delegated or out of scope**
The following are tested under their own requirements and are not reassessed here: the `coverage.tests` and `coverage.examples` error rules, the `coverage.history` window, and the details of `finish_search.inputs`.

text: :::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Outline inputs recorded from selected search snippets under {cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs` MUST count alongside mandatory inputs and additional reads. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{req} discovery
Habeas MUST find the references of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`
in project source files, where {cite}`requirements.references.reference_contexts`
says they count, and MUST fail with the source file and line if a
name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped
roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Reference discovery MUST
consider exactly the project sources that source-access policy permits under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`: in a Git worktree, files present in
the Git index, including staged new files; outside Git, all project files; in
both cases excluding the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories, `.git`
and `target` directories at any depth, and paths disallowed by
{cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`. Evidence snapshots and
generated build output MUST therefore not be counted as source references.
:::{req} util
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. A citation of
`habeas:util` MUST cover its item under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.
:::{req} finish_search.inputs
For each tag selected by a valid `finish_search` call, the harness MUST record
its `file`, `item`, and structural hash as an outline input under
{cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` before acknowledging that call.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} definition

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace and the header option lines of {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
:::{req} coverage.tests
Every Rust function carrying a test attribute, `#[test]` or an attribute whose
path ends in `test` such as `#[tokio::test]`, including those in Cargo
integration-test targets, MUST carry a `{test}` reference to a requirement or
named example under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`, in a comment
attached to it or within its body. A test function without one MUST be a
validation error naming its file, line, and name.
:::{req} coverage.examples
Every Cargo example target, each `.rs` file directly under the package's
`examples/` directory, each `examples/<name>/main.rs`, and each `[[example]]`
`path` in `Cargo.toml`, MUST `{cite}` a named example of the book under
{cite}`requirements.examples.definition` in a comment in that file. An example
target without one MUST be a validation error naming the file.
:::{req} coverage.report
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST report the number
of nodes without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, except items inside a module
named `tests`, using the following summary:
```text
N nodes have coverage warnings. Use `status --coverage` to see them.
The summary MUST report zero when no nodes have warnings. Default output MUST
NOT list individual coverage warnings or coverage-history details, including
with `status --all` or `status --verbose`.
`habeas status --coverage` MUST list every warning, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, and report incomplete coverage history when applicable.
A warning MUST NOT fail validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read
Git history.
